walkthroughs.body_html:
Research Methods & Researching Society — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Research Methods & Researching Society brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Research Methods & Researching Society.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Weber's concept for empathetic understanding of social action is:
options: Anomie
Verstehen
Praxis
Alienation

Ethnography
Content analysis
The most important socialisation, happening in school.

mcqs.q: What is the postmodern view of identity?
options: It is a recent invention of capitalism.
Everyone has the same identity in postmodern society.
Identities are fluid, fragmented, and constructed through consumption and choice.
Identity is fixed by class, gender, and ethnicity at birth.

mcqs.q: What did Murdock claim about the nuclear family?
options: It is universal and performs four essential functions in all societies.
Learning facts in primary school.
It is the only valid family form and others are dysfunctional.
It is a recent invention of capitalism.
